message.content:
The sea isn’t one single shade—its “color” depends on many factors:

| Factor | Typical Effect |
|--------|----------------|
| **Depth** | Shallow water looks turquoise/greenish because it reflects sunlight more than absorbs it. Deeper water appears darker blue as light penetrates less. |
| **Sunlight angle & intensity** | Bright midday sun makes the surface sparkle white (sun glare) while low-angle sunrise/sunset gives warm hues like orange‑pink. |
| **Water clarity / turbidity** | Clear waters show vivid blues; murky or algae‑rich seas look greenish or even brownish due to suspended particles. |
| **Substrate** | A sandy bottom may reflect yellowish tones; rocky bottoms can give a deeper, richer blue. |
| **Atmospheric conditions** | Overcast skies reduce contrast, making the sea appear grayish. |

So when people say “the sea is blue,” they’re usually referring to clear, deep ocean under bright daylight—a rich azure hue—but the actual appearance varies widely across locations and time of day.
